title: Rib cage tissue and joints
summary: Simulate slow tests of costal cartilage, ribs, rib-spine joints and sternum; report moduli, failure loads, joint rotations and load-deflection curves.
simulate: Build the specimen: cartilage beam, cylinder or slice; rib segment or whole rib; rib with its two vertebrae; sternum with cartilages.
Fix as tested: clamped rib end, potted ends (pinned-pinned), simple supports, or fixed vertebrae.
Apply the stated load slowly (quasi-static): bending, torsion, compression, indentation, pure moment, rib tension or dead weights.
Use nominal stress (force / undeformed area) and nominal strain (ΔL / L0).
Report the output as defined: modulus, failure value, ROM, moment at angle, or deflection at each load.

outputs.label: Elastic modulus
outputs.definition: Elastic modulus = slope of nominal stress vs nominal strain, or from beam / Hertz theory as stated (MPa)

outputs.label: Shear modulus
outputs.definition: Shear modulus from the torque-twist slope and section geometry (MPa)

outputs.label: Compressive strength
outputs.definition: Peak nominal compressive stress = peak force / undeformed area (MPa)

outputs.label: End displacement at fracture / D0
outputs.definition: End-to-end displacement at fracture / initial end-to-end span D0 (-)

outputs.label: Initial stiffness
outputs.definition: Initial slope of force vs end displacement, 0-5% of D0 (N/mm)

outputs.label: Modulus of rupture
outputs.definition: Modulus of rupture = peak bending stress from beam theory (MPa)

outputs.label: Joint range of motion
outputs.definition: Joint rotation between -M and +M (range of motion), rib relative to the vertebrae (deg)

outputs.label: Moment at given rotation
outputs.definition: Moment at the stated joint rotation, from the mean moment-angle curve (Nm)

outputs.label: Displacement
outputs.definition: Rib-head translation relative to the vertebrae under 28 N rib tension (mm)

outputs.label: Pin deflection in load direction
outputs.definition: Pin displacement in the load direction under the dead weight (mm)

notes: Quasi-static only (slow ramps or dead weights); the instantaneous (viscoelastic-fit) cartilage modulus was removed.
Stress = nominal (force / undeformed area), strain = nominal (ΔL / L0), as in Ghezelbash et al. 2020 J Biomech 102:109463.
Gradischar and Lebschy (shared donors) report medians, not pooled; Schultz 1974b curves are one cadaver; Duprey curves come from the published mean polynomial.
agent_prompt: You are given a model of the human rib cage (costal cartilage, ribs, costovertebral and costotransverse joints, sternum). For every task, build the specimen named in the inputs, fix it as tested (clamped, potted pinned-pinned, simply supported, or vertebrae fixed) and apply the stated load quasi-statically: bending, torsion, tension, unconfined compression or indentation of cartilage; three-point or end-to-end bending of ribs; pure moments, rib tension or dead weights on the joints and sternum. Use nominal stress (force / undeformed area) and nominal strain (change in length / initial length). Report the requested output: modulus, failure force or deflection, range of motion between the moment limits, moment at the given rotation, or pin deflection at each load. Return one JSON object following answer_format (task id -> {output key: value}); use null for tasks you cannot simulate.
